\section{Complete results}\label{app:results}
% Generated from the evaluation-run CSVs (see the % src: comment after each table). Do not edit numbers by hand.
This appendix lists the complete numbers behind every result in the paper: all variants, inference modes, domains, per-object and per-seed breakdowns, medians, accuracies at thresholds, flip statistics, and each pre-registered criterion with its outcome. Each subsection names the evaluation run its tables are read from. Unless stated otherwise, values are 3-seed means, $\pm$ is the sample standard deviation over seeds, errors are in degrees and accuracies and failure rates are fractions. \emph{Synth.\ val} is the clean synthetic validation set, \emph{synth.\ val-aug} the same images with the fixed EXP-109 augmentation (one copy, seed 1000), used as a generalisation proxy for selection; lightbox and sunlamp are test-only. acc@$k$ is the fraction of images with error below $k^\circ$; $>$90 and $>$150 are the fractions above $90^\circ$ and $150^\circ$. In flip-transition columns, \emph{fixed} is the share of the reference system's $>$150$^\circ$ errors that become $<$20$^\circ$, and \emph{broken} the share of its $<$20$^\circ$ predictions that become $>$150$^\circ$; the reference counts are seed means and can be fractional. Two evaluation passes of the same trees can differ in the second decimal (\eg the sunlamp PoE + orbit error is 12.28 in EXP-112 and 12.25 in EXP-113--117); each table uses a single run and the values are not reconciled.

\subsection{EXP-109: augmentation and orbit voting (locked recipe)}\label{app:exp109}
\paragraph{Question.} Can the frozen-feature tree generalise better to real images when (A) training is augmented (photometric + exact in-plane roll), (B) finer $16{\times}16$ DINOv3 tokens are used, or (C) predictions are made consistent over the four in-plane rotations of the test crop (orbit voting)? Arm A + C is the locked recipe used throughout the paper.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome} (selection on synthetic val and val-aug; real domains descriptive; ``beats'' means a 3-seed mean difference larger than the larger seed std):
\begin{itemize}
\item A helps generalisation (PoE val-aug below the clean EXP-036 tree, clean synth.\ val not worse): \textbf{PASS}. Val-aug 9.75\,$\pm$\,0.07 vs 30.84\,$\pm$\,0.40; clean 4.86\,$\pm$\,0.03 vs 5.54\,$\pm$\,0.07.
\item B (tokens16) helps generalisation: \textbf{FAIL}. Val-aug 30.51\,$\pm$\,0.20 vs 30.84\,$\pm$\,0.40, a difference within the seed std.
\item C (orbit voting) helps on top of its base: \textbf{PASS} on both bases. On A: val-aug 5.82 vs 9.75, clean 3.87 vs 4.86; on the clean EXP-036 trees: val-aug 19.84 vs 30.84.
\item Real domains: descriptive only (no threshold).
\end{itemize}
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-109_real_domain_aug_tokens16_orbit.md (criteria); outputs/experiments/EXP-109_real_domain_aug_tokens16_orbit/RUN-20261016-014754-seed0/metrics/metrics.csv (numbers)
\paragraph{Label convention.} The roll label transform $q'=\mathrm{Exp}(-\theta d)\otimes q$ was derived from the camera geometry and verified before any augmented training: the projected Tango points match the warped crop to 0.34\,px mean (1.05\,px p95), the exact label error is 0.06$^\circ$ mean (0.20$^\circ$ p95, 1.14$^\circ$ max), and the round trip is within 0.004$^\circ$; the other three candidate transforms are off by 94--242\,px.
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-109_real_domain_aug_tokens16_orbit.md (Amendment 2026-10-15)
\paragraph{Single branches} (training-run evaluation, greedy, synth.\ val / lightbox / sunlamp): DINOv3 + augmentation 4.84 / 22.5 / 22.0 against 5.34 / 37.1 / 41.5 without; MoGe-2 + augmentation 17.6 / 40.6 / 59.5 against 16.7 / 43.7 / 60.6; tokens16 DINOv3 5.37 / 37.9 / 39.7.

\subsection{EXP-117: orbit distillation}\label{app:exp117}
\paragraph{Question.} Can a single-view tree, distilled from the orbit system of the same seed and variant (teacher: orbit over the three training views, 24 candidates weighted by the softmax of the orbit-product score; loss $L_{\mathrm{GT}}+\beta H$ with $\beta=1$), recover part of the orbit gain at one-view cost? Three students per seed: a DINOv3 student from the DINOv3-only teacher, and DINOv3 and MoGe-2 students from the PoE teacher.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Distillation helps (student single-view greedy val-aug below the base greedy by more than the larger seed std, clean synth.\ val not worse; DINOv3 primary, PoE secondary): \textbf{PASS}. DINOv3 9.33\,$\pm$\,0.18 vs 9.88\,$\pm$\,0.22; PoE 9.22\,$\pm$\,0.10 vs 9.75\,$\pm$\,0.06; clean synth.\ val DINOv3 4.57 vs 4.84, PoE 4.56 vs 4.85 (better).
\item Retention $=$ (base greedy $-$ student greedy)/(base greedy $-$ base orbit), descriptive, synth.\ val / val-aug / lightbox / sunlamp: DINOv3 43\% / 15\% / 18\% / 22\%; PoE 30\% / 13\% / 28\% / 23\%.

\subsection{EXP-118: 6-DoF with a translation block on SPEED+}\label{app:exp118}
\paragraph{Question.} Can the locked architecture be extended to full 6-DoF with a translation block on the tree's tokens, using the SPACE-HOP translation target~\cite{dutta2026spacehop} unchanged, and does the block add information beyond the ground-truth box without hurting rotation? Arms: J (tree and block trained jointly), F (block on the frozen EXP-109 tree), and B (box only, no image: object centre at the box centre, depth at the training mean of $U_z$). The PoE translation is the mean of the two branches' predictions; orbit translation averages the four back-rolled views.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.}
\begin{itemize}
\item The block adds information beyond the box (J and F synth.\ val $E_T$ below box-only by more than the larger seed std, PoE and DINOv3): \textbf{PASS}. Box only 0.561\,m; J DINOv3 0.078 (1 view) / 0.059\,m (orbit); J PoE 0.111 / 0.093\,m.
\item Joint training does not hurt rotation (J synth.\ val rotation within the larger seed std of EXP-109 arm A, or better): \textbf{PASS}. PoE greedy 4.78 vs 4.85, PoE orbit 3.86 vs 3.87, DINOv3 greedy 4.78 vs 4.84 (F's rotation is the EXP-109 arm A tree).
\item Real domains: descriptive.
\end{itemize}
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-118_translation_6dof.md (criteria); outputs/experiments/EXP-118_translation_6dof/RUN-20261020-031510-seed0/metrics/metrics.csv (numbers)

\subsection{EXP-113: tree vs.\ flat Hopf classifier}\label{app:exp113}
\paragraph{Question.} Does the hierarchical Tesseract tree improve on a flat classifier over a count-matched Hopf grid (SPACE-HOP's 10,923 directions $\times$ 12 rolls $=$ 131,076 anchors), with identical features, augmentation, budget and orbit inference? The flat head uses the same trunk plus a 131k-way linear layer (36.1\,M trainable parameters per branch, 33.6\,M in the head, vs.\ 2.4\,M for the tree), geodesic soft targets over the 32 nearest anchors with the tree's leaf temperature, and scores an orbit candidate by the log-probability of its nearest anchor. This comparison confounds hierarchy and grid (\cref{app:exp127}).
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.}
\begin{itemize}
\item The tree improves on the flat grid on synth.\ val (PoE + orbit primary, PoE greedy secondary): \textbf{PASS}. Orbit 3.87\,$\pm$\,0.03 vs 7.53\,$\pm$\,0.01; greedy 4.85\,$\pm$\,0.03 vs 8.95\,$\pm$\,0.06.
\item Same rule on synth.\ val-aug: \textbf{PASS}. Orbit 5.82\,$\pm$\,0.10 vs 9.80\,$\pm$\,0.09; greedy 9.75\,$\pm$\,0.06 vs 15.06\,$\pm$\,0.20.
\item Real domains: descriptive. The tree has the lower mean and median in every real comparison; the flat head with orbit voting has fewer $>$150$^\circ$ errors on lightbox.
\item The withdrawal clause (flat matches the tree) was not triggered.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{EXP-114: orbit scoring rules}\label{app:exp114}
\paragraph{Question.} With the same four views and the same 32 back-mapped candidates, does the orbit-product score add something beyond ordinary test-time-augmentation voting? Rules: greedy (view 0 only); max-confidence (candidate with the highest beam log-probability in its own view); top-1 vote (5$^\circ$ Gaussian-kernel vote among the four views' top-1); weighted vote (kernel vote over all 32 candidates weighted by per-view normalised probability); orbit product (sum over views of the tree log-likelihood of the candidate mapped into each view).
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.} The product passes if its 3-seed mean is below the best of the three simpler rules by more than the larger seed std (PoE primary, DINOv3 secondary).
\begin{itemize}
\item Synth.\ val: \textbf{FAIL} for PoE (product 3.87\,$\pm$\,0.03 vs best other, weighted vote (32), 3.46\,$\pm$\,0.03); \textbf{FAIL} for DINOv3 (4.21\,$\pm$\,0.04 vs weighted vote (32) 3.71\,$\pm$\,0.05).
\item Synth.\ val-aug: \textbf{PASS} for PoE, marginally (5.82\,$\pm$\,0.10 vs weighted vote (32) 5.98\,$\pm$\,0.13); \textbf{FAIL} for DINOv3 (6.25\,$\pm$\,0.12 vs weighted vote (32) 6.30\,$\pm$\,0.06).
\item Real domains: descriptive; the product has the lowest mean on both real domains for both variants.
\item Consequence (pre-registered clause): no product-specific claim; the claim is multi-view orbit consistency over hierarchical candidates.
\end{itemize}
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-114_orbit_scoring_rules.md (criteria); outputs/experiments/EXP-114_orbit_scoring_rules/RUN-20261016-231825-seed0/metrics/metrics.csv (numbers)
Cost: the weighted vote needs the per-view beam scores and a $32\times32$ angle matrix ($<$0.1\,ms per image); the product re-scores 32 candidates in 4 views (8.2\,ms DINOv3-only, 15.3\,ms PoE at batch 1, \cref{app:tab:exp112time}).

\subsection{EXP-115: augmentation ablation}\label{app:exp115}
\paragraph{Question.} Which part of the augmentation causes the real-domain flip recovery: photometric only, in-plane roll only, or both, each with and without orbit inference? The clean EXP-036 trees are the no-augmentation reference.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome} (orbit product, synth.\ val-aug):
\begin{itemize}
\item Roll augmentation matters (both beats photometric only): \textbf{PASS}. PoE 5.82\,$\pm$\,0.10 vs 11.16\,$\pm$\,0.08; DINOv3 6.25\,$\pm$\,0.12 vs 8.68\,$\pm$\,0.19. Caveat: val-aug itself contains random rolls and favours roll-trained arms by construction.
\item Photometric augmentation matters (both beats roll only): \textbf{PASS}. PoE 10.49\,$\pm$\,0.17 for roll only; DINOv3 12.58\,$\pm$\,0.03.
\item Orbit gain by arm (greedy $-$ orbit, PoE, val-aug; descriptive): none (clean) 11.00, photometric only 5.91, in-plane roll only 7.06, both (EXP-109 A) 3.93.
\item Real domains (descriptive): photometric only matches the combined recipe with orbit voting; roll only stays close to the clean trees. The real-domain gain is therefore attributed to photometric augmentation plus orbit voting (\cref{tab:aug}).
\end{itemize}
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-115_augmentation_ablation.md (criteria); outputs/experiments/EXP-115_augmentation_ablation/RUN-20261017-121554-seed0/metrics/metrics.csv (numbers)

\subsection{EXP-116: roll-consistent tree}\label{app:exp116}
\paragraph{Question.} Can training learn the cross-view consistency that orbit voting enforces at test time, at single-view cost? Arms (per branch, 3 seeds): C1 paired views of the same image, GT loss only (data control); C2 a transported consistency loss on the leaf distribution (a standard equivariance regulariser); T the hierarchical transported loss at every tree level ($\lambda=1$, beam 8); A the EXP-109 base recipe. Transport maps each view's beam-8 leaves into the other view's frame with the exact roll.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.}
\begin{itemize}
\item T beats A, C1 and C2 on single-view greedy val-aug (DINOv3 primary, PoE secondary) without hurting clean synth.\ val: \textbf{FAIL}. DINOv3: T 9.57\,$\pm$\,0.06 vs A 9.88\,$\pm$\,0.22, C1 10.04\,$\pm$\,0.21, C2 9.43\,$\pm$\,0.14; PoE: T 9.17\,$\pm$\,0.12 vs C2 9.08\,$\pm$\,0.05. T beats A and C1 but not C2.
\item Consistency improves over A and C1 (DINOv3 val-aug cons.@10): \textbf{PASS}. T 0.603 vs A 0.554, C1 0.541; C2 is higher still (0.621).
\item Real domains: descriptive; differences between A, C2 and T are within the seed std. By the pre-registered rule no hierarchical-transport claim is made.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{EXP-104: flip audit}\label{app:exp104}
\paragraph{Question.} Do the $\sim$180$^\circ$ real-domain errors of the clean trees come from a bug (encoder/decoder, metric, rotation convention, augmentation), from chart seams, from hierarchical routing, or from visual near-symmetry of the spacecraft? Analysis only (no training, no selection), on the frozen EXP-036 seed-0 greedy predictions of each branch.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.} This audit was a user-requested side analysis with no pass/fail criterion; each candidate cause has a test and a verdict. Encoder/decoder, metric, convention and augmentation bugs are ruled out; chart seams and hierarchical routing are not the main cause (flat Hopf heads on the same features flip as often or more: P($>$150$^\circ$ $|$ $>$90$^\circ$) $=$ 0.42--0.58 vs.\ 0.35--0.40 for the tree on the same subset); visual near-symmetry is the main cause. For uniformly random wrong rotations about 20\% of errors above 90$^\circ$ fall in 165--180$^\circ$; the observed share is 36--41\%. Among the tree's top-8 beam paths, one lies within 20$^\circ$ of the ground truth for 86\% of lightbox images.

\paragraph{Decoder round trip.} Over all ground-truth rotations, decoding the encoded path gives a maximum error of 5.78$^\circ$ (NumPy decoder) and 5.78$^\circ$ (GPU decoder used at inference), mean 2.51$^\circ$ (the depth-5 cell-centre quantisation); manifest paths match the encoder for a fraction 1.000 of rows, and $q$ and $-q$ encode identically (yes).

\subsection{EXP-064: T-LESS, SYMSOL-T and YCB-V (incl.\ zero-shot)}\label{app:exp064}
\paragraph{Question.} Do the locked recipe and its components (orbit voting, MoGe-2 fusion) carry over to other objects when per-object trees are retrained with the unchanged recipe? Datasets: T-LESS~\cite{hodan2017tless} (7 objects, PBR validation scenes 45--49, real BOP19 test targets), SYMSOL-T (5 shapes, LiePose split~\cite{hsiao2024liepose}, 20k training images per shape, 2k held-out validation, test-5k) and YCB-V~\cite{xiang2018posecnn} (6 objects, real training videos only, held-out sequences for validation, keyframes for test). T-LESS and SYMSOL-T use the symmetry-aware error (continuous symmetries discretised in 10$^\circ$ steps); YCB-V uses the raw error (no symmetry metadata in this release). These are the single-label (A0) trees. A zero-shot arm evaluates the frozen SPEED+ trees without retraining.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.} Per dataset, fusion helps if the object-balanced PoE validation mean is below DINOv3-only by more than the larger seed std; test is reported for every arm. Zero-shot transfer is claimed only if the frame-free pair error is below its uniform-chance level by more than the seed std.
\begin{itemize}
\item T-LESS: \textbf{PASS}. PoE vs DINOv3 validation, greedy 12.30\,$\pm$\,0.13 vs 12.67\,$\pm$\,0.06; orbit 9.25\,$\pm$\,0.07 vs 9.94\,$\pm$\,0.06.
\item SYMSOL-T: \textbf{FAIL}. PoE vs DINOv3 validation, greedy 3.87\,$\pm$\,0.03 vs 3.78\,$\pm$\,0.03; orbit 2.65\,$\pm$\,0.01 vs 2.61\,$\pm$\,0.00.
\item YCB-V: \textbf{FAIL}. PoE vs DINOv3 validation, greedy 73.52\,$\pm$\,6.81 vs 64.32\,$\pm$\,11.63; orbit 74.06\,$\pm$\,7.43 vs 62.99\,$\pm$\,2.40.
\item Zero-shot: the pre-set rule is literally met on T-LESS and SYMSOL-T, but a post-hoc constant-prediction control (one rotation for every image, same pairs) is better than the frozen trees on T-LESS (88.7$^\circ$) and YCB-V (57.8$^\circ$); on SYMSOL-T the control equals chance (53.8$^\circ$) and the signal comes from the cube only. No general zero-shot transfer is claimed (\cref{tab:zeroshot}).
\end{itemize}
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-064_broader_object_validation.md (criteria, constant-prediction control); outputs/experiments/EXP-064_broader_object_validation/RUN-20261019-063238-seed0/metrics/object_balanced.csv; outputs/experiments/EXP-064_broader_object_validation/RUN-20261019-233710-seed0/metrics/object_balanced.csv; outputs/experiments/EXP-064_broader_object_validation/RUN-20261019-224920-seed0/metrics/object_balanced.csv

\subsection{EXP-106: symmetry-aware training targets}\label{app:exp106}
\paragraph{Question.} For symmetric objects, does a multi-path target, in which every equivalent rotation gets its own tree path and the probability mass is divided between them, predict better than the single annotated label (A0) or a canonical label (A1, the equivalent rotation closest to identity)? A2 averages the recipe's geodesic soft-target loss over the equivalent rotations (all of them when $|S|\le8$, otherwise 8 drawn per row and step); it reduces exactly to A0 for objects without symmetry. Per-object trees, 2 branches, 3 seeds, the locked recipe otherwise. A0 is the EXP-064 tree set re-evaluated under this experiment (identical numbers). Arm K (Kurz corner formulation) and the best-fit stage were not run.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.} Criterion 1 (as amended before any run): A2's object-balanced validation PoE greedy mean is below the better of A0 and A1 by more than the larger seed std. Evaluated here from the CSVs against that rule.
\begin{itemize}
\item T-LESS: \textbf{PASS}. A2 10.82\,$\pm$\,0.11 vs A1 11.46\,$\pm$\,0.04 (A0 12.30\,$\pm$\,0.13). Descriptive, PoE orbit product: A0 9.25\,$\pm$\,0.07, A1 10.71\,$\pm$\,0.03, A2 8.28\,$\pm$\,0.05.
\item SYMSOL-T: \textbf{PASS}. A2 2.72\,$\pm$\,0.01 vs A1 3.40\,$\pm$\,0.01 (A0 3.87\,$\pm$\,0.03). Descriptive, PoE orbit product: A0 2.65\,$\pm$\,0.01, A1 9.73\,$\pm$\,0.05, A2 2.10\,$\pm$\,0.01.
\item Criterion 2 (best-fit re-ranking): not run. Criterion 3: test reported for every arm below.
\end{itemize}

\clearpage

\paragraph{Leaf quantisation on SYMSOL-T.} Post hoc, the symmetry-aware error of the ground-truth rotation's own depth-5 leaf centre on the SYMSOL-T test set is 2.31$^\circ$ on average (cone 2.02, cube 2.50, cylinder 2.02, icosahedron 2.51, tetrahedron 2.51); A2's orbit error can fall below it because the tree may select the leaf closest to any equivalent rotation.
% src: paper/SOURCES.md (SYMSOL-T leaf-quantisation floor, post hoc 2026-10-22)

\subsection{EXP-122: YCB-V with synthetic training renders}\label{app:exp122}
\paragraph{Question.} The EXP-064 YCB-V trees, trained on real videos only, fit their training frames but did not generalise. Does adding the standard \texttt{data\_syn} renders (composited onto real frames drawn only from the training sequences; at most 12,000 per object, same visibility rule) make the frozen-feature tree work? One arm (B: real + synthetic), the EXP-064 real-only trees as control; validation and test rows unchanged.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria and outcome.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Synthetic data helps (B's validation PoE orbit-product mean below real-only by more than the larger seed std), evaluated here from the CSVs against that rule: \textbf{PASS}. 12.74\,$\pm$\,1.03 vs 74.06\,$\pm$\,7.43.
\item Test numbers for every variant and mode, and per-object test errors: below.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{EXP-127: hierarchy vs.\ flat on the same grid}\label{app:exp127}
\paragraph{Question.} EXP-113 compared the tree with a flat classifier over a \emph{different} grid, so hierarchy and discretisation were confounded. EXP-127 trains two further flat heads with the identical recipe and orbit inference: FL over the tree's own 131,072 leaf centres (scoring a candidate by the probability of its Tesseract cell, as the tree does), and FH over a balanced Hopf grid (1,771 Fibonacci directions $\times$ 74 rolls $=$ 131,054 anchors). The tree arm reuses the EXP-109 arm-A checkpoints; orbit distillation is excluded from all arms.
\paragraph{Pre-registered criteria.} A difference passes if the 3-seed synthetic-val means differ by more than the larger seed std. (1) Hierarchy, T vs.\ FL, PoE + orbit primary: if FL ties or wins, the claim that the tree's advantage comes from hierarchical prediction is withdrawn. (2) Discretisation, FL vs.\ FH, descriptive. (3) System, T vs.\ FH, PoE + orbit. (4) Real domains and cost descriptive. A tree-reproduction gate against EXP-113 seed 0 (within 0.02$^\circ$) precedes the trainings.
\paragraph{Outcome.} \emph{Pending}: the trainings and the evaluation are queued and have not run; no criterion has been evaluated. Only the quantisation floor, which needs no learning, is available.

\subsection{Pending experiments: EXP-119, EXP-124, EXP-126}\label{app:pending}
The following pre-registered experiments are running or queued at the time of writing. No result is reported for them except the completed ground-truth-crop reference evaluation of EXP-124.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{EXP-119, orbit distillation on T-LESS and SYMSOL-T.} Base arm: per dataset, the EXP-106 target with the lowest validation PoE greedy mean; DINOv3-only and PoE students as in EXP-117 ($\beta=1$). Criterion: student single-view greedy validation mean below the base arm's by more than the larger seed std (DINOv3 primary). Status: queued; no run directory exists. The distillation rows of \cref{tab:sym} and \cref{tab:tless_sota} remain blank.
\item \textbf{EXP-124, SPEED+ with a synthetic-only detector and the official score.} A YOLO11s detector trained on synthetic images only provides the crops; systems S1 (EXP-117 PoE students + orbit, EXP-118 joint DINOv3 translation, orbit mean), S2 (EXP-118 joint PoE) and S3 (EXP-117 DINOv3 student + EXP-118 joint DINOv3 translation). Criteria are descriptive: the detected-crop score per domain, and the detection gap (detected $-$ GT-crop score). Status: the detector training is running (the first attempt was aborted by the memory guard and the queue retried with identical settings); no detected-crop result exists, and the last row of \cref{tab:spp_sota} remains blank. The ground-truth-crop reference evaluation of the same systems with the same code is complete and is reported below.
\item \textbf{EXP-126, translation on T-LESS, SYMSOL-T and YCB-V.} Frozen trees plus a SPACE-HOP translation block per object; criterion: DINOv3 validation $E_T$ (orbit mean) below the box-only baseline by more than the larger seed std. Status: queued; no run directory exists.
\end{itemize}
% src: outputs/reports/EXP-119_xobj_orbit_distillation.md; outputs/reports/EXP-124_speedplus_detected_official_score.md; outputs/reports/EXP-126_translation_xobj.md; outputs/experiments/EXP-124_speedplus_detected_official_score/RUN-20261029-145416-seed0/status.json (state: running)

\paragraph{EXP-124 ground-truth-crop reference.} Its pre-registered gate requires the GT-crop S1 rotation to reproduce EXP-117 (11.21/11.09$^\circ$ on lightbox/sunlamp) and the S1 translation to reproduce EXP-118 joint DINOv3 (0.185/0.183\,m). The run gives 11.21/11.09$^\circ$ and 0.185/0.183\,m, so the gate passes. The score is the official SPEED+ score~\cite{park2022speedplus}: the mean over images of $e_q$ (rad) $+$ $e_t=\|\hat t-t\|/\|t\|$, with the precision floors applied per component; \emph{joint rule} applies the floor to the sum (a check; the sources disagree on the rule).
